newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Mapfre Brazilian unit 1996 net sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: Mapfre Brazilian unit 1996 net sharply lower.

text.p: Brazilian insurance company Vera Cruz Seguradora SA, majority-owned by Spanish insurer Mapfre Vida SA, said its 1996 net profit dropped 90.3 percent to 535,000 reais against 5.5 million reais in 1995.

The company said in a statement its poor 1996 results were due to factors such as an increase in overall insurance claims and operating losses in its life insurance portfolio due to higher marketing costs and claims.
Moreover, the company said it has injected 6.7 million reais in capital into its life insurance and pension unit Vera Cruz Vida e Previdencia SA.
In 1997, the company aims to break even in operating terms by controlling internal costs, cutting marketing costs and improving financial investments.
Vera Cruz Seguradora SA's net worth rose 52 percent last year to 111 million reais against 83.9 million reais in 1995.
Mapfre's Brazilian unit Mapfre do Brasil owns 94.1 percent of Vera Cruz Seguradora SA capital.
